answers.implementation_then_now: The law was the same on both dates. No provision prohibits force as a means of stopping entry, so the answer is the lowest option on both dates and implementation does not apply.
answers.sourcing_note: SINALEVI's current versions of Ley 7410 (version 19 of 19) and Ley 8764 (version 19 of 19) were read. Ley 7410 art. 10(d) and Ley 8764 arts. 18 and 64 carry no amendment notes. Ley 7410 art. 6 was last reformed by Ley 10061 (2021), before the window. The only 2023–2025 change to Ley 8764 found was Ley 10493 (5 June 2024), which touches fees in arts. 33 and 241 and has nothing to do with force. The version histories of Decrees 31463-SP and 38756-MGP were not reopened.

answers.sourcing_note: Ley 7410 art. 10(d) was read in the current SINALEVI text: 'Emplear la fuerza solo cuando sea estrictamente necesario y en la medida en que se requiera para el desempeño de sus funciones.' It carries no amendment note. Ley 8764 art. 64 has no amendment note either. The version history of the constitutional articles was not reopened, but no amendment to arts. 21 or 40 is known in the window.

answers.implementation_then_now: 2023 rating: the 2023 TIP Report (covering 2022) records 38 identified victims, 18 of them foreign. It notes written identification procedures used by immigration authorities and 75 temporary residence permits for victims, and reports no penalisation of victims, but rural officials often did not know the referral procedures. 2026 rating: the 2025 TIP Report (covering 2024) records 53 certified victims, at least nine of them foreign, and again no reported penalisation. It notes similar gaps: certification centralised in San José, labour inspectors referring few cases, and NGOs assisting victims the government never certified. The pattern did not change, so the rating is Usually on both dates.

answers.sourcing_note: Ley 9095 art. 70 was read in SINALEVI version 4 of 4 and carries no amendment note, so it has been unchanged since 2012. The amendments to Ley 9095 in that text are Ley 9545 (2018), Ley 9726 (2019) and Ley 10886 (18 March 2026). The last is after 1 January 2026 and touches arts. 10, 16 and others, not art. 70. Ley 8764 art. 249 carries no amendment note. The practice evidence covers trafficking victims, not smuggled migrants.
answers.starting_answer_concern: The exemption is express only for trafficking victims (art. 70: 'Las víctimas del delito de trata de personas no son punibles penal o administrativamente...'). For smuggled migrants it follows from their non-criminalisation under art. 249, and no clause covers, for example, their use of false documents. A reviewer may consider the 'Yes' generous for smuggled migrants.
answers.notes: Ley 10886 of 18 March 2026 amended Ley 9095 after the window and did not touch art. 70. Ley 10493 (June 2024) amended fee paragraphs of Ley 8764 arts. 33 and 241, not art. 249 or the administrative treatment of irregular entry. The evidence on smuggled migrants is thin: neither TIP report addresses their prosecution.
